title: Traffic Fork Controller and Tenant Quotas for Safe Inflight Evaluation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need a robust, tenant-aware way to run inflight evaluations (forked live traffic to evaluation clusters) without risking production SLAs or runaway costs. Existing ad-hoc mirroring paths are brittle: unclear per-tenant cost exposure, no unified sampling policy, and limited isolation for KV cache/side-effects.

Goal: Implement a Traffic Fork Controller (TFC) that can route a configurable fraction of live requests to evaluation replicas with per-tenant quotas, stratified sampling, adaptive budget throttles, provenance headers, and automatic mitigation (throttle/disable) on SLO or cost regressions. The TFC should plug into API gateway routing, emit billing-grade metrics, and be controllable from the Console (canaries/A-B/experiments).

Scope: core controller + API hooks + metrics + console controls. Not included in this ticket: UI polish for Console experiment builder (follow-up PM ticket).

Design highlights: 1) Per-tenant budget tokens: tenants allocate monthly evaluation budget; controller deducts cost estimate per-eval request and enforces hard/soft limits. 2) Stratified sampler: sampling rules support tenant, route, model-version, and payload-size strata to avoid skewed evaluation populations. 3) Isolation guarantees: evaluation cluster runs in read-only mode, KV cache is shadowed (no writes back to prod cache); any requests with side-effects are detected by filter and dropped from fork. 4) Adaptive budget throttle: controller reduces sampling rate when cumulative evaluation cost > X% of allocated budget or when tail latency regresses beyond threshold. 5) Provenance and lineage: forked requests include X-RI-FORK and X-RI-EVAL-ID headers; Console can trace tokens to evaluation results. 6) Auto-mitigation rules: configurable triggers (latency percentile shift, error delta, quality regression from eval harness) that auto-pause forks and create alerts/tickets.

Why different from previous work: previous shadow/mirroring tickets focus on basic duplication and sampling. This implementation combines tenancy-aware costing and live circuit-breaking with explicit cache isolation and standardized provenance so experiments are auditable and billable.
acceptance_criteria: A Traffic Fork Controller service is deployed to staging and can fork traffic for a single test tenant with a configurable sampling rate
Per-tenant budget tokens are debited by an estimated cost per-eval request and enforced (soft warning at 80%, hard stop at 100%)
Stratified sampling rules support at least tenant, route path prefix, and input token-length bins
Forked requests carry provenance headers (X-RI-FORK, X-RI-EVAL-ID) and are visible in trace logs and Console experiment view
Evaluation-side writes to prod cache or downstreams are suppressed; any attempt is logged and counted as a safety violation
Controller emits billing-grade metrics: eval_tokens_consumed, eval_request_count, eval_error_rate, eval_latency_p50/p95/p99 per-tenant
Auto-mitigation triggers exist for: +10% p95 latency increase vs baseline, +2% absolute error-rate increase, or crossing tenant budget hard limit; triggers pause forks and create an incident ticket
tasks: Design and document TFC API and config schema (routes, strata, budgets, triggers)
Implement controller service that subscribes to gateway sampling decisions and forks requests to evaluation endpoints
Integrate cost-estimation logic that maps token estimate to budget debit per tenant
Enforce cache isolation: implement read-only shadow cache and detection for side-effecting ops
Emit metrics + tracing hooks and wire to Console experiment panels
Add automated mitigation logic and alerting playbook
End-to-end tests: synthetic traffic generator, cost burn test, regression injection test
